items.title: Middle East Update 24th July: Disruption “Doubling Up”?
items.synopsis: After last week’s return to “closure” transit levels at Hormuz, this week has seen disruption “spread” to the Red Sea with the first Houthi attacks on ships in 2026. Initial datapoints suggest a drop in VLCCs crossing the Bab El Mandeb (but not a “closure”) alongside some signs of re-routing. In this Analysis we review latest trends and plans to boost energy security by developing “bypass” options.

items.title: Middle East Conflict: Offshore & Energy Context & Updates - 4th March 2026
items.synopsis: Further updates on the fifth day of the Middle East conflict, with further vessels and maritime infrastructure attacked, Strait of Hormuz vessel transits remaining very limited, supply chain disruption growing and signs of shipping market gains.

items.title: Middle East Conflict: Update No. 3 - 4th March 2026
items.synopsis: Further updates on the fifth day of the Middle East conflict, with further vessels and maritime infrastructure attacked, Strait of Hormuz vessel transits remaining very limited, supply chain disruption growing and signs of shipping market gains.

items.title: Car Carrier Trade & Transport 2025
items.synopsis: The annual review of the car carrier sector from Clarksons Research, Car Carrier Trade & Transport 2025, has today been released, including coverage of car carrier charter markets, car industry and seaborne car trade trends, trends in the car carrier fleet, asset and newbuilding market trends, and market supply-demand projections

items.title: Container Port Congestion Back In The Spotlight
items.synopsis: Back in 2021/22, port congestion and broader logistical disruption were major features of the container shipping markets, helping drive freight rates (and shipper costs) and vessel charter rates to unprecedented levels. Having wound down across 2H-2022 & 2023, container port congestion this year, following the onset of the disruption in the Red Sea, is having a notable impact once again.

items.title: US And Chinese Port Fees: Taking Stock...
items.synopsis: Shipping has again it seems been at the “frontline” of geo-politics this week, with US port fees on Chinese related vessels commencing, rapid introduction of Chinese “counter measures” and heated discussions at IMO around the pace and direction of emissions reduction. In this week’s Analysis, we try to take stock after a “chaotic” week, aiming to provide a framework for assessing impacts.

items.title: Chinese Port Fees On US-Linked Vessels: 14th October 2025 Update No. 2
items.synopsis: An update on the Chinese port fees on US-linked vessels after China announced exemptions for Chinese-built ships. Both China's fees on US-linked ships and the USTR's fees on Chinese linked ships have come into effect as of today.

items.title: Chinese Port Fees On US-Linked Vessels: 12th October 2025 Update
items.synopsis: China has announced imminent port fees for US linked vessels, mirroring USTR measures, coming in the context of broader US-China negotiations that remain dynamic.

items.title: Q1 2026 Shipping Market Review
items.synopsis: Geopolitical events again dominated the agenda for shipping through first quarter 2026, with major disruption and complex market conditions. Alongside the unprecedented interruption to Middle East cargo flows, shipping markets (especially ‘energy’ segments) have been elevated (our cross-sector ClarkSea Index averaged $36,865/day in Q1), albeit with uncertainty “clouding” the outlook.

items.title: Q1 2026 Shipping Market Review - Summary Statistics
items.synopsis: A summary of the key shipping market trends and statistics in Q1 2026.

items.title: Seaborne Oil Trade: Bouncing Back...
items.synopsis: While oil trade volumes faced headwinds through 2024 and early 2025, with our seaborne oil trade indicator in negative year-on-year territory for most of this period, momentum started to shift in mid-2025 amidst particularly strong improvements in crude trade volumes. Here we review some of the key drivers of the recent recovery...

items.title: US Seaborne Energy Exports: A Mixed Picture?
items.synopsis: The rapid increase in oil and gas production and exports in the United States has been one of the key tanker and gas carrier demand trends over the past decade, with the US on track to become the largest seaborne “energy” exporter this year. However, following a period of consistent growth, a more nuanced situation is developing with variation between cargoes emerging.

items.title: Seaborne Oil Products Trade: In It For The Long Haul?
items.synopsis: The average haul of global seaborne oil products trade has trended upwards over the last five years, increasing by an estimated 11% across 2018-22. However, gains in average haul have accelerated notably this year, largely on the back of Russia-related trade flow shifts. Here we take a closer look at the recent shifts in global products trade patterns.

Guinea Bauxite & Iron Ore Exports Update: May 2026
items.synopsis: Guinea bauxite exports have continued to show rapid growth in 2026, up 29% y-o-y across Jan-Apr, whilst iron ore exports from Simandou have started to ramp-up, supporting Capesize markets to hit a two-year high.

items.title: Guinea Bauxite Exports & Bulkcarrier Congestion: July 2025
items.synopsis: Bauxite exports from Guinea have continued to grow rapidly so far in 2025, providing growing demand for Capesize vessels which handle ~90% of shipments. Exports in 1H 2025 were up by 35% y-o-y to 93mt, with around 82% of this volume being shipped long-haul to China.

items.title: Bulkcarrier Markets Enjoying The Summer Sun
items.synopsis: The dry bulk market has made a strong start to 2026, with earnings recently hitting unseasonal multi-year highs, building momentum going into the summer. Strength has been led by Capesizes, kicking on again after a robust 2H 2025, while improving ‘sub-Cape’ performance has broadened the rally. Here we put recent bulker market strength into context and weigh up the drivers.

items.title: Russia-Ukraine Conflict - Vessel & Infrastructure Attacks Update - 14th Aug 2026
items.synopsis: Conflict between Russia and Ukraine in focus again recently amid attacks on vessels, ports and infrastructure in the Black Sea which are increasingly impacting vessel activity and trade, particularly in oil and grain

items.title: A Bumper Year For Grain Trade (So Far)
items.synopsis: Grain trade has delivered a bountiful harvest for dry bulk shipping so far in 2026, led by record shipments from major exporters in the Americas. Strong volumes on long-haul routes into Asia have supported tonne-mile demand growth and provided a tailwind for mid-sized bulkers in particular. However, there are a range of complexities to watch ahead, from geopolitics to climate patterns…

items.title: Bulkcarrier Market Outlook - August 2026
items.synopsis: Bulkcarrier markets have been relatively firm in 2026 so far, with weighted sector earnings averaging ~$18,000/day in the year to date, up ~50% y-o-y; demand has been robust across 2026 to date, while strong long-haul Atlantic-to-Asia exports have provided additional tonne-mile support; overall, the bulkcarrier sector is on track for a positive year

items.title: EU Review of the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS)
items.synopsis: On 17th July 2026, the EU Commission published its review of the EU ETS, along with its proposals for future improvements to the regulation. EU countries and the European Parliament will now propose their own revisions and negotiate the final amendments, a process which is expected to take place over the next couple of years.

items.title: Containership Market Update: Q3 2025
items.synopsis: Rapidly evolving US trade policy has shaped a volatile year so far for container shipping, with trade volumes, freight markets and industry sentiment fluctuating significantly against a backdrop of a fluid and uncertain geopolitical and economic outlook

items.title: IMO ‘Mid-Term’ Measures
items.synopsis: Last month, the IMO reached a landmark agreement on the next phase of regulation to drive shipping’s emissions reduction, amid targets for ‘net zero’ to be reached by 2050. Shipping is now the first sector to have an agreed global carbon pricing mechanism, and the deal marks a further ramp-up in the environmental regulatory landscape impacting the shipping industry.

items.title: Containership Market Update: Q2 2025
items.synopsis: Container markets have seen divergent trends in 2025 after firm gains in 2024, with freight rates weakening, whilst the charter market has shown resilience amid tight tonnage availability. Weaker underlying fundamentals and building tariff impacts suggest potential for softer container shipping markets ahead, albeit with major uncertainty and a range of scenarios possible.

items.title: Newbuilding Investment Running ‘Hot’
items.synopsis: The newbuilding market has seen a strong flow of activity in 2024 so far, with the volume of tonnage ordered up by 70% on the ten year run-rate. In terms of the value of investment, the trend has been even more acute, with 2024 already representing the fourth strongest year on record, exceeded only by the mid-2000s order boom.
